title: Bananas (per lb)

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: Historical evidence shows 8–12% sales drop when a competitor opens nearby; one past occurrence, noise-adjusted estimate shrunk toward 1.0 due to low frequency.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 438.2. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increase to $0.68 (+1.5%) is small and recent history shows no meaningful lift at this level (week 2026-09-28: 524 units at $0.68, vs baseline 438.2 → x1.20, but no repeat pattern). A competitor opening across the street introduces demand risk. Past similar events (e.g., store openings nearby) reduced sales by 8–12% on average. The noise-adjusted effect is uncertain (one past occurrence), so shrink toward 1.0. No seasonal ramp or trend override. The classical model’s 1.00 is appropriate as a starting point.

brief:
PRODUCT: Bananas (per lb) | category Produce | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 0.68 (+1.5% vs regular price 0.67)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 438.2 | 5%-95%: 312.1 - 556.5 | 10%-90%: 346.2 - 529.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-21% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
